name: Agenium

hlido_opinion.headline: Two Persian-language solo-operator tools with genuinely careful consent design — a week of silent observation before the sales assistant sends anything — held back by crypto-only billing and no evidence of use.
hlido_opinion.body: Agenium ships two independent services for freelancers and small business owners: Coach, an execution system that turns goals into projects, stages and daily tasks, checks in on a chosen cadence, and adapts to observed behaviour rather than serving a static task list; and DM, a Telegram direct-message assistant that answers customers on the business's behalf. The consent architecture in DM is better than most products ten times its size. It opens in Shadow mode, where replies are composed but never sent — the first week it sends nothing at all and only learns. Suggest mode drafts a reply that the owner approves or edits with one button, and nothing goes out unapproved. There is a global kill switch, it learns from the owner's real replies rather than a scripted scenario, and it needs no premium or business Telegram account. The site states the governing rule plainly: where being helpful and not making a mistake collide, not making a mistake wins. That is a defensible design philosophy for an agent acting in someone's name, and it is the reason this is not scored lower. The rest is thin. The surface is Persian-only with an English toggle we did not verify, subscription is payable solely in TON and USDT on TRON with no conventional payment path, and there are no customers, usage figures, pricing detail, team information or third-party validation of any kind. Both services are described but neither is demonstrated.

tier_rationale: FADING (58) for consent design that is genuinely careful — Shadow mode sending nothing for the first week, Suggest mode requiring per-message approval, a global kill switch, and an explicit rule that avoiding mistakes beats being helpful. Held at FADING because nothing on the surface shows the products in use: no customers, usage, pricing detail, team or validation; crypto-only billing (TON/USDT-TRON) with no conventional payment path narrows the addressable audience sharply; and the surface is effectively Persian-only.
what_it_does_well: Shadow mode composes replies but sends nothing for the first week — observation before action, by default
Suggest mode requires explicit per-message approval; nothing is sent without it
Global kill switch stops the whole system with one command
Learns from the owner's own real replies rather than a pre-written script
Works on any Telegram account — no premium or business account required
States its governing principle openly: where helpfulness and correctness collide, correctness wins
Coach adapts to observed behaviour (when the user stalls, when they progress) rather than serving a static task list
what_it_fails_at: Subscription is payable only in TON and USDT on TRON — no card, bank or conventional payment path
No customers, usage numbers, pricing figures, team information, or third-party validation
Surface is effectively Persian-only; an English toggle exists but was not verified
Neither service is demonstrated — both are described in feature terms with no evidence of operation
Two quite different products (personal execution coach, customer-facing sales assistant) share one thin surface
A DM assistant answering customers in a business's name carries real reputational risk that the safeguards mitigate but cannot remove
best_for: Persian-speaking freelancers and solo operators who want an accountability system that adapts to their behaviour
Small businesses on Telegram wanting after-hours replies with human approval kept in the loop
Users comfortable paying in TON or USDT
not_recommended_for: Anyone who cannot or will not pay in cryptocurrency
Businesses needing a non-Persian interface or multilingual customer handling
Buyers who require evidence of production use before letting software answer customers in their name

red_flags.note: Subscription is payable only in TON and USDT on TRON. This is disclosed clearly rather than hidden, but the absence of any conventional payment path is a material constraint and, for some buyers, a trust signal in itself.

evidence_urls.claim: Two independent services: Agenium Coach (execution system) and Agenium DM (Telegram sales assistant)
Shadow mode composes replies without sending; the first week sends nothing and only learns
Suggest mode requires one-button owner approval before any message is sent
Global kill switch halts the entire system with a single command
Subscription payable in TON and USDT (TRON network) only
Customers, usage figures, pricing detail, or team information

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: End-user services delivered through Telegram and a web app. No public API, CLI, MCP surface or SDK, so this is a product a person uses rather than a component another agent can drive.

checklist.evidence: 'A system to execute with. An assistant to sell with.' (translated)
'Start with Agenium Coach' / 'Start with Agenium DM'
Payment rails named (TON, USDT-TRON) but no prices published
Feature descriptions only — no demo, screenshots of use, or customer evidence

summary: Two Persian-language solo-operator tools with genuinely careful consent design — a week of silent observation before the sales assistant sends anything — held back by crypto-only billing and no evidence of use.
